nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Yakushima is among the wettest places in Japan, with several thousand millimetres of rain a year, which keeps the mountain forest constantly damp.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives forest growth and the plankton of the surrounding sea.

nodes.name: Kuroshio warm current
nodes.desc: A warm ocean current flows past the Ryukyu islands and keeps the sea around the island warm, supporting its plankton and marine life.

nodes.name: Forest soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Thin, wet forest soil holds the nutrients that the cedars, shrubs and ferns draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen wood, leaves, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil and sea.

nodes.name: Yakusugi cedar
nodes.desc: Japanese cedar that grows very old on the island; the ancient trees called yakusugi are a hallmark of the forest and shelter many mosses and ferns.

nodes.name: Rhododendron
nodes.desc: Flowering shrubs, with several endemic species on the island, that grow on the high slopes and ridges.

nodes.name: Filmy ferns
nodes.desc: Thin-leaved ferns that thrive in constantly humid air; ferns are among the most recorded plants on the island.

nodes.name: Mosses and liverworts
nodes.desc: The island has many rare mosses and liverworts that carpet trunks, rocks and the forest floor in the damp air.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae at the base of the food web of the sea around the island.

nodes.name: Yakushima macaque
nodes.desc: A subspecies of the Japanese macaque that eats young leaves, seeds, flowers, fruit and insects, with its diet shifting with season and temperature.

nodes.name: Yakushika (sika deer)
nodes.desc: The island's sika deer is its own subspecies, along with the macaque one of the island's only native large animals. It browses the forest floor.

nodes.name: Japanese wood pigeon
nodes.desc: A dark pigeon of island forests that feeds mainly on fruits, berries, leaves, buds and conifer seeds.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed jellyfish and many other sea animals.

nodes.name: Raccoon dog
nodes.desc: Common on the island though not native. It digs into sea turtle nests and takes baby turtles.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: A bold omnivore that scavenges carrion and, like other crows, takes sea turtle eggs and hatchlings.

nodes.name: Ghost crab
nodes.desc: Beach crabs that scavenge and hunt on sand and prey on turtle eggs and hatchlings.

nodes.name: Jellyfish
nodes.desc: Drifting predators of plankton and a main food of loggerhead turtles at sea.

nodes.name: Loggerhead sea turtle
nodes.desc: Yakushima is the largest nesting ground for loggerheads in the North Pacific. Adults eat jellyfish and shellfish; eggs and hatchlings are eaten by crabs, crows and raccoon dogs.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: A big shark that often eats adult sea turtles, which it is well equipped to bite through.
